sections.title: Overview: A Passover of Restoration and All-Israel Renewal

blocks.text: This chapter records Hezekiah's initiative to restore centralized temple worship through a kingdom-wide Passover celebration. The king consults with his officials and the Jerusalem assembly to organize the festival, then dispatches messengers with letters throughout the land, extending the invitation not only to Judah but explicitly to the northern tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh. The resulting proclamation demonstrates the narrative's interest in reconstructing an all-Israel community centered on the Jerusalem temple, with renewal of covenant relationship at its heart.

Hezekiah's council determines to celebrate Passover in the second month rather than the first, because the priests have not had sufficient time to sanctify themselves and the people have not yet gathered to Jerusalem. The assembly approves this adjustment, and a public proclamation is dispatched reaching from Beer-sheba in the south to Dan in the north, calling the scattered people to Jerusalem for the observance. This geographic breadth underscores the attempt to summon Israel as a unified entity across territorial divisions.
